description.narrative: The program follows a sequenced reform pathway to support Uzbekistan's objectives of macroeconomic stability and inclusive growth by strengthening public sector efficiency, fiscal sustainability, and accountability. Reform actions are structured around three pillars: (i) strengthening fiscal management through program-based budgeting, fiscal risk monitoring, debt transparency, and climate-informed public investment planning; (ii) improving SOE governance by aligning legal frameworks with market principles, enhancing financial transparency, and promoting fair competition; and (iii) enhancing public sector accountability through robust audit systems and reinforced anti-corruption legislation and enforcement. These reforms aim to address structural inefficiencies and deliver measurable improvements in service delivery, market competitiveness, and institutional integrity. Original outcome indicators have been retained with elevated targets to reflect expanded ambition, while new indicators capture deeper reforms in tax policy and administration, investment climate, SOE restructuring, social protection, and anti-corruption enforcement. The program continues to reflect strong reform commitment and coherence with its foundational design and strategic objectives.

Action 1: In line with the Green Economy Strategy 2022-2030, the government: (i) approved and adopted Implementation of Measures Aimed at Improving the State Investment Management System of the Republic of Uzbekistan 2025-2028 per IMF PIMA and Climate-PIMA recommendations; (ii) established unified PPP regulations requiring climate change and gender impact assessments and to strengthen fiscal sustainability; (iii) established a cap of $6.5B on the maximum value of all new signed PPP projects in the Law "On the State Budget for 2025" and approved and adopted regulations for managing state fiscal obligations from PPPs. Target value: 3
Action 2: In line with the PFM Strategy and Action Plan 2025-2030 to strengthen fiscal discipline, the government: (i) adopted and initiated implementation of program-based budgeting in 2 ministries and procedures for green budgeting, and for gender-responsive budgeting (GRB) principles; (ii) published the Fiscal Strategy 2026-2028, which includes a fiscal risk statement covering SOEs, SOBs, and PPPs in alignment with IMF fiscal transparency standards; and (iii) implemented a new DMFAS module to record government debt and sovereign guarantees to SOEs for credit risk monitoring. Target value: 3
Action 3: In line with the Fiscal Strategy 2025-2027, the government approved (i) amendments to the Tax Code introducing inflation-adjusted tax to preserve the real value of tax revenue covering excise tax; water resource usage tax and land tax; (ii) amendments to the Tax Code to tax the digital economy more effectively by increasing the profit tax rate and the turnover tax rate on e-commerce; (iii) market value as the basis for property taxation; (iv) a progressive VAT compensation scheme to benefit low-income households registered in the Unified Register of Social Protection; and (v) amendments to the Tax Code to align with WTO requirements, including unified excise tax rates and removal of exporter tax incentives. Target value: 3
Action 4: To counter aggressive tax planning and profit shifting by multinational entities, the government joined the Inclusive Framework on Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) and committed to implementing the minimum standards. Target value: 3
Action 5: To strengthen tax administration in line with the main directions of tax policy for the medium-term period as part of the Fiscal Strategy 2025-2027, the State Tax Committee implemented: (i) an automated income tax filing system for individuals and legal entities, including sex-disaggregated data across all taxpayer categories; (ii) a key performance indicator system to monitor the activities of tax administrations at the central and regional levels; and (iii) an IT-based risk assessment system for tax compliance and tax audits. Target value: 3
Action 6: To strengthen social protection, the government: (i) established the National Social Protection Agency to oversee all social programs across government; (ii) submitted to Parliament the Law "On State Social Insurance" providing benefits for disability, maternity and childbirth, and unemployment; and (iii) approved digital Social Card reducing the costs and streamlining the process to access social benefits. Target value: 3

Policy 2: SOE governance and operations improved. NA
Action 2: To strengthen competitive markets, the government: (i) enacted the Law "On Competition" and normative legal regulations introducing stricter merger thresholds, dominance criteria, superior negotiating power rules, antimonopoly compliance, and financial sanctions; (ii) amended the "Code of Administrative Responsibility" introducing penalties for anti-competitive actions and non-compliance with antitrust orders; (iii) adopted sector-specific regulation ensuring fair access to digital markets; and (iv) approved the Competitive Development Index to assess the state of the competitive environment in the economy and submitted activity report to Parliament. Target value: 1
Action 3: To create a level playing field for the private sector and SOEs and align national legislation with WTO regulations, the government: (i) enacted Law abolishing the state unitary enterprise as legal form of commercial organization and reorganized, restructured all state-unitary enterprises; and (ii) exclusive rights previously granted to SOEs were reformed to establish equal competition, non-discrimination, and market-based operations in key sectors, in line with WTO accession requirements. Target value: 1
Action 4: To strengthen corporate governance of SOEs, the government: (i) enacted the Law reforming the composition and governance of supervisory boards of SOEs, establishing clear criteria for the selection of independent board members to ensure impartiality, transparency, and accountability; (ii) approved updated Rules of Corporate Governance for SOEs aligned with the OECD Guidelines to enhance transparency, accountability, and board effectiveness; (iii) to increase diversity in largest state owned joint-stock SOE's, requiring at least 15% female supervisory board representation by 2027; (iv) mandated all Public Interest Entities to adopt international financial reporting standards; and (v) conducted corporate governance assessments aligned with the OECD guidelines in selected SOEs to assess compliance status with corporate governance principles. Target value: 1
Action 5: To improve operational efficiency, financial performance, and service delivery of the state-owned water utility: (i) the government approved the 2025-2026 Roadmap for Improving Drinking Water and Wastewater Supply, launching a nationwide reform agenda to modernize infrastructure, digitize utility operations, and transform JSC Uzsuvtaminot into a commercially viable and accountable service provider through stronger planning, investment oversight, and performance management; (ii) the government launched a national water metering program to improve billing accuracy, reduce water losses, and promote efficient use; and JSC Uzsuvtaminot; (iii) adopted new policies on the competitive selection of independent directors to strengthen corporate governance and oversight; (iv) approved policies on anti-corruption, conflict of interest, code of ethics, and whistleblower protection to reinforce institutional integrity; and (v) rolled out a public engagement campaign to build support for tariff reforms and encourage responsible water use. Target value: 1
